source.section: PDF page 60 Schedule CA (540) instructions, Line 5a and 5b ('Generally, no adjustments are made on this line'; no subtraction for another state's government pension); Form 540 lines 13 to 19 and 31 to 33 (PDF pages 39-40); PDF page 13 Line 18 standard deduction chart and Line 31; PDF page 75 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Single, 62, California resident: a New York State and Local Retirement System pension 60,000 and wages 20,000; federal AGI = 80,000. California has no subtraction for another state's government pension, so the New York pension is taxed in full. Form 540 line 13 federal AGI = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 64,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtractions: none (the New York State pension is taxed as included in federal AGI, Schedule CA line 5, PDF page 60). Form 540 line 14 = 0.00. Additions (line 16): 0.00. Line 15 = line 17 California AGI = 80,000.00 - 0.00 = 80,000.00. Line 18 California standard deduction (single, PDF page 13 chart) 5,706.00. Line 19 taxable income = 80,000.00 - 5,706.00 = 74,294.00. Tax on 74,294.00 by the projection's brackets: 11,079.00 x 1% = 110.79; 15,185.00 x 2% = 303.70; 15,188.00 x 4% = 607.52; 16,090.00 x 6% = 965.40; 15,182.00 x 8% = 1,214.56; 1,570.00 x 9.3% = 146.01; total 3,347.98. Line 31: the form uses the Tax Table for taxable income of 100,000 or less; the row 74,251-74,350 gives 3,349 (formula result kept in expected). Line 32 exemption credits: federal AGI 80,000.00 is not more than 252,203.00, so no AGI limitation; line 7 personal 1 x 153 = 153.00; line 9 senior 0 x 153 = 0.00; line 32 = 153.00. Line 33 = 3,347.98 - 153.00 = 3,194.98; no other credits (lines 34 to 47 nil), line 48 = 3,194.98. State income tax = 3,194.98.
accepted_approximations: Taxable income of 100,000 or less is taxed by the Tax Table (100-dollar rows, tax at the row midpoint); the projection uses the schedules' exact arithmetic.
